newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-SAO PAULO GO ON ANOTHER GOALSCORING SPREE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SAO PAULO GO ON ANOTHER GOALSCORING SPREE.

text.p: Sao Paulo continued their amazing revival by beating arch-rivals Palmeiras 4-2 in the Sao Paulo championship at the weekend.
The win followed an 8-1 demolition of Juventus in the same tournament last Sunday and a 5-2 hammering of America on Thursday.
Nineteen-year-old striker Dodo, who scored hat-tricks in each of the previous games, added two more as Sao Paulo recovered after going behind early on.

The result made Sao Paulo, who have suddenly found their goalscoring touch after a mediocre start, mathmatically sure of a place in the four-team final play-off, along with Corinthians, who guaranteed their place in midweek.
Both teams are in group two.

Defending champions Palmeiras look certain to qualify from group one despite the defeat. The battle for the last place lies between Portuguesa, last year's runners-up in the Brazilian championship, and Santos.
Portuguesa maintained their two-point advantage over Santos by beating Portuguesa Santista 2-1 away while Santos won 2-0 at Mogi Mirim. Each team has three games left.
Botafogo won the second stage of the Rio de Janeiro championship after drawing 0-0 with Fluminense before an 80,000 crowd to give themselves an excellent chance of taking the overall title.
Botafogo also won the first stage of the tournament and will take the title automatically if they win the third and last stage, which starts next week.

Otherwise, they will meet the winners of the third stage in a playoff. But, under the complicated rules of the tournament, they would start a first-to-six-points series of games with a four-point advantage by virtue of having won two stages.
Fluminense, who needed to win the game to wrest the second stage from Botafogo, were livid at having a first-half penalty appeal turned down by referee Carlos Elias Pimentel.

"The referee is fat, he's not running and he's got no physical preparation. He is watching the game from the middle of the pitch," said Fluminense official Jose Roberto Wright, himself a former World Cup referee.
